clue.text: Using breeze with skill, one can fly

parts.note: a breeze is moving air
craft is skill, as in a craftsman's

explanation.surface: A glider pilot or a kite flyer rides the wind with expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes, gliders and helicopters are all machines built for flight, which is what the word covers.

clue.text: Dirty place on front of eye can cause an eyelid problem

parts.note: a pigsty, or any filthy place

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of eye

explanation.surface: A warning that grime near the eye can lead to an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a medical fact, since a dirty eyelid really can cause the swelling the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small painful swelling at the edge of the eyelid caused by an infected gland.

clue.text: It'll make someone late!

parts.note: surface reading: something that causes a person to arrive behind time
setter's reading: late in the sense of the late Mr Smith, that is, dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like unpunctual, but in obituaries the late so-and-so is someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing someone turns them into the deceased, which is the obituary sense of the adjective.

clue.text: A batsman is the one doing no work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, the batsman currently facing the bowling
second meaning: a worker who has walked out in an industrial dispute

explanation.surface: A dig at a lazy cricketer who stands around while others toil.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing the bowler is called the striker; the other meaning is someone on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both the cricketer receiving the ball and an employee withholding labour during a dispute.

clue.text: Possibly ring Gay about student wanting fish

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece wraps the other
possibly suggests one arrangement among several, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of phoning a person called Gay for advice on a fish-hungry student.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters spell GRAYING, and the learner's L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family, prized by anglers in clear rivers.

clue.text: Is man having painting in study causing dismay?

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
taken as written
he is the pronoun for a man
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A query about whether a man with a picture hanging in his study is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to discourage them and sap their spirits, a close synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Cancel part of model eternity ring order

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of the words that follow, not all of them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of model and the start of eternity

explanation.surface: A shopper calls off a jewellery order for an eternity ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to remove or strike out, as when a keyboard key wipes text or a manager scraps a plan.

clue.text: Beware of water vapour corrosion

parts.note: mist is fine water vapour in the air
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A warning sign about damp causing metal to corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wary or suspicious of something is to doubt it and keep on guard, much like being told to beware.

clue.text: Shoving her about in river

indicators.note: shoving one thing in pushes it inside another
about can mean all around and jumbled, so those letters are moved

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pushing a woman into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is the great European river flowing from Switzerland through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Top male expert comes round

indicators.note: to come round something is to encircle it, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A leading specialist pays a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the highest point or peak of achievement, the very summit of something.

clue.text: Why is Adele replacing this on a typewriter?

definitions.note: 'this' stands for the answer: the part found on a typewriter

indicators.note: replacing means putting back in different places, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled office worker asks why a colleague is changing a part of the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisywheel is the replaceable disc of spokes, each tipped with a character, used in electric typewriters and early printers.

clue.text: Stout girl's parent

parts.note: stout means fat
her is the possessive for a girl

explanation.surface: A rather unkind description of a young woman's dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the dark beer, but here it is the adjective for heavy-set.
explanation.definitionFit: A male parent is called a father, so this is a plain dictionary synonym.

clue.text: eat captain to shark

parts.note: SOURCE ERROR: the served clue has lost its first letter; the setter's word is 'Beat', and to beat is to pound or batter
a captain is the head of a team or crew

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is thrashed and thrown to the sharks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as served reads 'eat', but the printed Guardian clue began 'Beat'; only that verb supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammerhead is a species of shark with a flattened, T-shaped head and widely spaced eyes.

clue.text: Dreadful, steamier Eastern states

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible mess, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about the awful humid heat of countries in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates are territories ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf, which lie in the Middle East.

clue.text: Batsman may be baffled!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cricket dismissal where the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of his ground

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease is left confused.
explanation.walkthrough: Being out this way is a cricket dismissal: the keeper knocks the bails off while the batsman has wandered from his crease.
explanation.definitionFit: One participle names both a way of losing one's wicket and the state of being unable to find an answer.

clue.text: Note name, sex and breed

parts.note: E is a musical note
N is the abbreviation for name
sex in the sense of male or female

explanation.surface: A list of the details a form asks for: name, sex and breed of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to produce or give rise to, which the verb also means, as in hatred bred by fear.

clue.text: He thinks I'm great!

parts.note: surface reading: someone pleased to hear another person admires the speaker
setter's reading: the speaker's own opinion of himself, voiced in the first person

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as boasting about an admirer, but the person who thinks 'I'm great' is the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person preoccupied with his own importance holds exactly this view of himself.

clue.text: In a dress ruined by fish

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its original form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's outfit spoiled by a fishy accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines are small oily fish of the herring family, often sold packed in tins.

clue.text: Conservative leader has a number to discipline

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Conservative
taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A Tory party chief has a handful of MPs to bring into line.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or subdue someone through punishment, a verb sense of discipline.

clue.text: Ability to withstand great pressure might

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the toughness of a material under load

explanation.surface: An engineer describes how sturdy a structure might prove under load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like the verb of possibility closing the sentence, but it is the noun for power.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a material's resistance to force and physical power or vigour.

clue.text: Objects when working nights

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and reorganised

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shift worker complains, or perhaps objects to the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' could be the verb for protesting, but it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Things are items or articles, plain physical objects, a direct noun synonym.

clue.text: Bit of a plan Arkwright made here

definitions.note: a place: where something was made

indicators.note: bit of says only a stretch of the following words is needed

parts.note: the letters run across the end of plan and the start of Arkwright

explanation.surface: Part of an industrial pioneer's scheme was carried out at this site.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright, the cotton-mill pioneer, helped plan the mills of New Lanark in Scotland, so the place really is where his plan was made.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a Scottish town beside the New Lanark mill village, a site of manufacturing history.

clue.text: Non-professional fellow is following minstrel's song

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a lay is a medieval ballad sung by a minstrel
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An amateur turns up as a fan of a wandering minstrel's music.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is someone without expert or professional training in a field, an amateur outsider.

clue.text: Fraud switches stone in attractive setting

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for attractive

parts.note: dishy is informal British for good-looking, here the setting that surrounds the gem

indicators.note: switches means changes over, so the letters swap positions

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller's con: a fake gem swapped into a pretty mount.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishy is British slang for attractive, usually of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is deception for gain, and the noun names the quality of being deceitful or untruthful.

clue.text: Having one in one's home was profitable

indicators.note: having something in one's home means holding it inside

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's flat or home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Taking in a lodger turned out to be a money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: When a venture paid, it yielded a return, so the past tense of pay fits a profitable outcome.

clue.text: Faint sound of a bucket?

indicators.note: sound of tells us to go by how a word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: faint means pale, as of a light colour

explanation.surface: A quiet clink from a bucket being set down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faint sound' reads as a quiet noise, but faint is a synonym for pallid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is an old-fashioned word for a bucket used to carry water or milk.

clue.text: Some taking ravens to the vet will be serious!

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so a stretch of the letters is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of taking and the start of ravens

explanation.surface: Bringing sick ravens to an animal doctor is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious both describe a solemn situation that gives cause for worry.

clue.text: One testing axe returned by a collier

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a tool handed back by a coal worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner sets or marks tests and inspects candidates, so is someone doing the testing.
